curiosities: Many DOS games asked for a Sound Blaster's port, IRQ and DMA settings before they would play a sound.
Commander Keen brought smooth side-scrolling to the PC with a technique called adaptive tile refresh.
Doom was released as shareware in December 1993, its first episode free to copy.
Some games were copy-protected with questions from the manual or code wheels in the box.
MS-DOS began as 86-DOS, which Microsoft bought from Seattle Computer Products.
It shipped with the IBM PC in 1981 as PC DOS.
Programs had 640 KB of conventional memory to work in.
The AdLib card of 1987 brought FM music to PC games, and the Sound Blaster of 1989 digital sound too.
VGA's mode 13h, 320 × 200 in 256 colours, was the standard for games of the early 1990s.
id Software's Wolfenstein 3D came out in 1992.
